72342-mr-jervis-vol-3-of-3.title: Mr. Jervis
72342-mr-jervis-vol-3-of-3.creator: B. M. Croker
72342-mr-jervis-vol-3-of-3.description: A book by B. M. Croker. When Mark Jervis came all eagerness to claim his supper dance from Miss Gordon, he saw at once that something was wrong. The merry smile--her greatest charm--he sought in vain upon her face; her expression was grave, almost stern. She was actually looking at him as if he was an absolute stranger.

arxiv-2108-07806.title: Simulation and estimation of an agent-based market-model with a matching engine
arxiv-2108-07806.creator: Ivan Jericevich, Patrick Chang, Tim Gebbie
arxiv-2108-07806.description: Abstract An agent-based model with interacting low frequency liquidity takers inter-mediated by high-frequency liquidity providers acting collectively as market makers can be used to provide realistic simulated price impact curves. This is possible when agent-based model interactions occur asynchronously via order matching using a matching engine in event time to replace sequential calendar time market clearing.

arxiv-2110-00835.title: Phase diagram in a one-dimensional civil disorder model
arxiv-2110-00835.creator: Ignacio Ormazábal, Felipe Urbina, Félix A. Borotto, Hernán F. Astudillo
arxiv-2110-00835.description: Abstract Epstein’s model for a civil disorder is an agent-based model that simulates a social protest process where the central authority uses the police force to dissuade it. The interactions of police officers and citizens produce dynamics that do not yet have any analysis from the sociophysics approach.

arxiv-2202-03968.title: Self-supervised Contrastive Learning for Cross-domain Hyperspectral Image Representation
arxiv-2202-03968.creator: Hyungtae Lee Heesung Kwon
arxiv-2202-03968.description: Abstract Recently, self-supervised learning has attracted attention due to its remarkable ability to acquire meaningful representations for classification tasks without using semantic labels. This paper introduces a self-supervised learning framework suitable for hyperspectral images that are inherently challenging to annotate.

arxiv-2204-01906.title: Dynatask: A Framework for Creating Dynamic AI Benchmark Tasks
arxiv-2204-01906.creator: Tristan Thrush, Kushal Tirumala, Anmol Gupta, Max Bartolo, Pedro Rodriguez, Tariq Kane, William Gaviria Rojas, Peter Mattson, Adina Williams, Douwe Kiela
arxiv-2204-01906.description: Abstract We introduce Dynatask: an open source system for setting up custom NLP tasks that aims to greatly lower the technical knowledge and effort required for hosting and evaluating state-of-the-art NLP models, as well as for conducting model in the loop data collection with crowdworkers.

arxiv-2312-03193.title: Conceptualizing the Relationship between AI Explanations and User Agency Conference: CHI Workshops ’23 April 23–28, 2023, Hamburg, Germany DOI: https://doi.org/10.1145/3334480.XXXXXXX
arxiv-2312-03193.creator: Iyadunni Adenuga Jonathan Dodge
arxiv-2312-03193.description: Abstract We grapple with the question: How, for whom and why should explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) aim to support the user goal of agency? In particular, we analyze the relationship between agency and explanations through a user-centric lens through case studies and thought experiments.

arxiv-2503-23339.title: A Scalable Framework for Evaluating Health Language Models
arxiv-2503-23339.creator: Neil Mallinar, A. Ali Heydari, Xin Liu, Anthony Z. Faranesh, Brent Winslow, Nova Hammerquist, Benjamin Graef, Cathy Speed, Mark Malhotra, Shwetak Patel, Javier L. Prieto, Daniel McDuff, Ahmed A. Metwally
arxiv-2503-23339.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Neil Mallinar, A. Ali Heydari, Xin Liu, Anthony Z. Faranesh, Brent Winslow, Nova Hammerquist, Benjamin Graef, Cathy Speed, Mark Malhotra, Shwetak Patel, Javier L. Prieto, Daniel McDuff, Ahmed A. Metwally. Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as powerful tools for analyzing and interpreting complex datasets. Recent studies demonstrate their potential to generate useful, personalized responses when provided with patient-specific health information that encompasses lifestyle, biomarkers, and context.

arxiv-2506-22261.title: Shortest Paths in Multimode Graphs
arxiv-2506-22261.creator: Yael Kirkpatrick, Virginia Vassilevska Williams
arxiv-2506-22261.description: Abstract In this work we study shortest path problems in multimode graphs, a generalization of the min-distance measure introduced by Abboud, Vassilevska W. and Wang in [SODA’16]. A multimode shortest path is the shortest path using one of multiple ‘modes’ of transportation that cannot be combined.

arxiv-2601-05910.title: Multi-Task Modeling for Engineering Applications with Sparse Data Thanks: Equal Contribution
arxiv-2601-05910.creator: Yigitcan Comlek*, R. Murali Krishnan*, Sandipp Krishnan Ravi*, Amin Moghaddas, Rafael Giorjao, Michael Eff, Anirban Samaddar, Nesar S. Ramachandra, Sandeep Madireddy, Liping Wang
arxiv-2601-05910.description: Abstract Modern engineering and scientific workflows often require simultaneous predictions across related tasks and fidelity levels, where high-fidelity data is scarce and expensive, while low-fidelity data is more abundant. This paper introduces an Multi-Task Gaussian Processes (MTGP) framework tailored for engineering systems characterized by multi-source, multi-fidelity data, addressing challenges of data sparsity and varying task correlations.

pmc-10658562.title: Evaluation of the relationship between ionized and total calcium concentrations in blood during the first week of lactation in dairy cows
pmc-10658562.creator: Imke Cohrs, Sophia Wächter, Lennart Golbeck, Walter Grünberg
pmc-10658562.description: BackgroundDiagnosis of subclinical hypocalcemia in cattle is based on concentration of total Ca ([TCa]) in serum or plasma below the reference range, with [TCa] serving as proxy for the concentration of ionized Ca ([iCa]).Hypothesis/ObjectivesTo investigate the relation between [iCa] and [TCa] in periparturient cows over time, and its association with various metabolites.AnimalsThirty periparturient dairy cows.MethodsProspective observational study.

pmc-11353060.title: The Metabolomic Footprint of Liver Fibrosis
pmc-11353060.creator: Diren Beyoğlu, Yury V. Popov, Jeffrey R. Idle
pmc-11353060.description: Both experimental and clinical liver fibrosis leave a metabolic footprint that can be uncovered and defined using metabolomic approaches. Metabolomics combines pattern recognition algorithms with analytical chemistry, in particular, 1H and 13C nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR), gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) and various liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS) platforms.

pmc-11458983.title: Quality by design for mRNA platform purification based on continuous oligo-dT chromatography
pmc-11458983.creator: Jixin Qu, Adithya Nair, George W Muir, Kate A Loveday, Zidi Yang, Ehsan Nourafkan, Emma N Welbourne, Mabrouka Maamra, Mark J Dickman, Zoltán Kis
pmc-11458983.description: Oligo-deoxythymidine (oligo-dT) ligand-based affinity chromatography is a robust method for purifying mRNA drug substances within the manufacturing process of mRNA-based products, including vaccines and therapeutics. However, the conventional batch mode of operation for oligo-dT chromatography has certain drawbacks that reduce the productivity of this process.

pmc-11547078.title: Impact of Reductive Stress on Human Infertility: Underlying Mechanisms and Perspectives
pmc-11547078.creator: Efthalia Moustakli, Athanasios Zikopoulos, Charikleia Skentou, Periklis Katopodis, Ekaterini Domali, Anastasios Potiris, Sofoklis Stavros, Athanasios Zachariou, Stefano Palomba
pmc-11547078.description: Antioxidants have a well-established effect on general health and are essential in preventing oxidative damage to cells by scavenging free radicals. Free radicals are thought to be neutralized by these substances, which include polyphenols, β-carotene, and vitamins C and E, reducing cellular damage. On the other hand, recent data indicates that consuming excessive amounts of antioxidants may have side effects.

pmc-11573756.title: Alginate-like exopolysaccharides extracted from different waste sludges exhibit varying physicochemical and material properties
pmc-11573756.creator: Zahid Ur Rehman, Masoud Ghaani, Ahmed Y. A. Mohamed, John Gallagher, Pascal E. Saikaly, Muhammad Ali
pmc-11573756.description: This study examined the influence of different wastewater treatment processes on the physicochemical properties of Alginate-Like Exopolymers (ALE) extracted from waste sludge. Sludge samples were collected from wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) processing both combined industrial and domestic wastewater, as well as domestic wastewater alone.

pmc-11583359.title: Fixation alters the physical properties of tumor tissue that regulate nanomedicine transport
pmc-11583359.creator: John D. Martin, Fotios Mpekris, Vikash P. Chauhan, Margaret R. Martin, Megan E. Walsh, Matthew D. Stuber, Donald M. McDonald, Fan Yuan, Triantafyllos Stylianopoulos, Rakesh K. Jain
pmc-11583359.description: To have the desired therapeutic effect, nanomedicines and macromolecular medications must move from the site of injection to the site of action, without having adverse effects. Transvascular transport is a critical step of this navigation, as exemplified by the Enhanced Permeability and Retention (EPR) effect in solid tumors, not found in normal organs.

pmc-11682766.title: Recent progress in camel research
pmc-11682766.creator: Ashraf M Abu-Seida, Marwa H Hassan, Abdulrahman Abdulkarim, Elham A Hassan
pmc-11682766.description: Background:Camelids play an important role in the preservation of ecosystems, biodiversity, food security, economic growth, adaptation to climate change, and cultural and social aspects. Therefore, the United Nations has named 2024 the International Year of Camelids (IYC).Aim:This study aimed to assess the recent progress in camel research and its citation effect as shown in the Scopus database in the IYC.

pmc-11738885.title: The Experience of International Medical Graduates (IMGs) at Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health Foundation Trust (BSMHFT): A Quality Improvement Project
pmc-11738885.creator: Shahnila Sohail, Tabassum Mirza, Muhammad Abiola, Anum Asim, Adedamola Adeyanju
pmc-11738885.description: AimsTo improve the overall experience of IMG Doctors at BSMHFT. To demonstrate this, we targeted an increase in percentage of doctors rating their experience as excellent in our survey.MethodsEmploying the “Model for improvement”, we co -produced all aspects of project with subject matter experts (IMGs). What are we trying to accomplish? We co-produced process map/aim.

pmc-12288947.title: A Notch signaling pathway-related gene signature: Characterizing the immune microenvironment and predicting prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-12288947.creator: Qingmiao Shi, Shuwen Jiang, Yifan Zeng, Xin Yuan, Yaqi Zhang, Qingfei Chu, Chen Xue, Lanjuan Li
pmc-12288947.description: Background and ObjectivesPrior studies have highlighted an escalating global burden of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The Notch signaling pathway regulates the initiation and development of HCC and determines the HCC prognosis.MethodsThe expression data of genes related to the Notch signaling pathway were acquired from public databases.

pmc-12511531.title: Molecular mechanisms underlying the neuroprotective effects of polyphenols: implications for cognitive function
pmc-12511531.creator: Justyna Godos, Giuseppe Carota, Giuseppe Caruso, Agnieszka Micek, Evelyn Frias-Toral, Francesca Giampieri, Julién Brito-Ballester, Carmen Lili Rodríguez Velasco, José L Quiles, Maurizio Battino, Fabio Galvano, Giuseppe Grosso
pmc-12511531.description: Polyphenols are naturally occurring compounds that can be found in plant-based foods, including fruits, vegetables, nuts, seeds, herbs, spices, and beverages, the use of which has been linked to enhanced brain health and cognitive function. These natural molecules are broadly classified into two main groups: flavonoids and non-flavonoid polyphenols, the latter including phenolic acids, stilbenes, and tannins.

pmc-13096716.title: Antimicrobial Peptides and Systemic Inflammation: A Network Analysis
pmc-13096716.creator: Fabiano Pinheiro da Silva, Francisco Garcia Soriano, Ludhmila Abrahão Hajjar
pmc-13096716.description: IntroductionAntimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are essential components of the innate immune system, exhibiting diverse mechanisms of action.ObjectiveThis study investigates the roles of cathelicidin (LL‐37), alpha‐defensins, and the S100 proteins S100A8 and S100A9 in systemic inflammation associated with sepsis, severe COVID‐19, and acute pancreatitis using whole‐blood bulk RNA‐sequencing data.

pmc-13145531.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A2111 AUGMENTING THE ACCURACY OF THE LOS ANGELES MOTOR SCALE FOR LARGE VESSEL OCCLUSION SCREENING WITH CONTINUOUS WAVE FUNCTIONAL NEAR-INFRARED SPECTROSCOPY
pmc-13145531.creator: Geeta Charan Duba, Francois Xavier Nshimiyimana, Nitin Kumar, Nabeela Khan, Brian Buck, Mahesh Kate
pmc-13145531.description: Background and aimsA Los Angeles Motor Scale (LAMS) score of 4-5 is employed in the pre-hospital setting to screen large vessel occlusion (LVO) with moderate sensitivity. We aim to evaluate the adjunctive role of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to the LAMS score in classifying patients with LVO using a deep learning architecture.

pmc-13148705.title: Migrant mothers’ experiences of postnatal depression in the UK
pmc-13148705.creator: Laetitia Rater, Debra Marais, Aisling Kelly, Pracheth Raghuveer, Pracheth Raghuveer, Pracheth Raghuveer
pmc-13148705.description: BackgroundDespite the majority of migrants coming to the UK for voluntary reasons such as study, work or family, few studies explore their experiences of mental health. Prevalence of postnatal depression (PND) is higher amongst migrant women compared with non-migrant women. This qualitative study aimed to explore voluntary migrant mothers’ experiences of postnatal depression (PND) in the UK.

uslaw-usc-t10-s2228.title: 10 U.S.C. § 2228 — Office of Corrosion Policy and Oversight
uslaw-usc-t10-s2228.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s2228.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part IV (Service, Supply, And Property); Chapter 131 (Planning And Coordination). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Office and Director.— (1) There is an Office of Corrosion Policy and Oversight within the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment. (2) The Office shall be headed by a Director of Corrosion Policy.

uslaw-usc-t6-s234.title: 6 U.S.C. § 234 — Preservation of Transportation Security Administration as a distinct entity
uslaw-usc-t6-s234.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t6-s234.description: United States Code, Title 6 (Domestic Security); Chapter 1 (Homeland Security Organization); Subchapter IV (Border, Maritime, And Transportation Security); Part C (Miscellaneous Provisions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, the Transportation Security Administration shall be maintained as a distinct entity within the Department.
